Data/Question Source: Psychiatric casebooks, diagnostic manuals, and specialized clinical guides (DSM-5-TR Clinical Cases, Stahl's Essential Psychopharmacology, 100 Cases in Psychiatry, etc.) manually curated by licensed psychiatrists into 5,188 QA items
Ground Truth (Reference answers): Expert-annotated answers based on reference text
Evaluation method: Automated grading for the closed-form tasks like MCQ/EMI/classification. LLM-as-judge framework (LLaMA 3.3 70B) that scores open-ended answers 0–100 for content similarity to the reference answer

Data/Question Source: 100 real patient questions from CounselChat forum spanning 20 common mental health topics
Ground Truth (Reference answers): Top-upvoted therapist replies serve as human baseline compared alongside LLMs
Evaluation method: 100 licensed mental health professionals rate each response across 6 clinical dimensions

Data/Question Source: 120 adversarial questions generated by clinicians designed to elicit failure modes observed in CounselBench-Eval
Ground Truth (Reference answers): Clear clinician-authored definitions and one in-context example per failure type
Evaluation method: 5 mental health professionals (separate from question authors) label each response for targeted failure

Data/Question Source: USMLE-mental: 727 mental-health MCQs extracted from MedQA (USMLE Steps 1–2), keyword-filtered then author-reviewed. Crisis Response QA: 153 items authored from IACP (2018) and NAMI (2018) crisis manuals, GPT-4 created incorrect answers and medical students reviewed each question
Ground Truth (Reference answers): MCQ answer key based on MedQA + reference manuals
Evaluation method: Automated accuracy against MCQ key

Data/Question Source: SMHD: Reddit posts from users with one or more diagnosed mental-health conditions plus matched controls; the 16 most mental-health-relevant posts per user are retained; 500 users sampled (single- and multi-label).
Ground Truth (Reference answers): Diagnoses associated with each SMHD user
Evaluation method: Automated classification accuracy againt diagnostic labels for each user
Population: Reddit users with self-reported mental health diagnoses and matched controls

Data/Question Source: D4: ~130 multi-turn doctor-patient dialogues annotated with depression risk and suicide risk scores by clinicians
Ground Truth (Reference answers): Clinician-assigned depression-risk and suicide-risk scores (0-3) per dialogue
Evaluation method: Automated accuracy against the clinician-assigned risk scores

Data/Question Source: PsyQA: Chinese online mental-health Q&A written by trained counselors/volunteers; 100 patient inquiries sampled, each paired with a support-strategy sequence.
Ground Truth (Reference answers): Professional mental health counselor responses serve as a human baseline alongside rubric-based empathy and safety ratings
Evaluation method: GPT-4 as judge for response quality and EPITOME empathy (validated against human ratings); 8 human raters (qualification unstated) on a subset; fine-tuned BERT for dialogue safety.

Data/Question Source: 196 psychiatric case vignettes: 135 published diagnostic case reports manually collected from medical literature and independently reviewed by seven psychiatrists; 61 fictitious vignettes authored by six doctoral-level clinicians from real-world clinical experience.
Ground Truth (Reference answers): Gold answer key: the foremost standardized DSM-5-TR diagnosis in each vignette was treated as the primary reference diagnosis.
Evaluation method: LLM: GPT-5-mini acted as an independent psychiatric adjudicator, matching each model’s five predicted DSM-5-TR diagnoses to the reference diagnosis. Metrics: top-1 accuracy, top-5 accuracy, recall@5, and mean reciprocal rank.
Population: Psychiatric case vignettes derived from published diagnostic reports and fictitious clinician-authored cases; demographic population characteristics not specified.

Data/Question Source: Randomly selected subset of 30 vignettes from the 196-vignette clinician-curated psychiatric case dataset.
Ground Truth (Reference answers): Gold answer key for diagnostic correctness: the vignette’s primary DSM-5-TR reference diagnosis. Evaluation method: Human: five board-certified psychiatrists, blinded to model identity, assessed each vignette-model output. Analyses included Fleiss’ kappa, ICCs, and mixed-effects logistic regression.
Population: Psychiatric case vignettes derived from published diagnostic reports and fictitious clinician-authored cases; demographic population characteristics not specified.

Data/Question Source: 150 single-best-answer psychiatry MCQs extracted from the Psychiatry Test Preparation and Review Manual; each item posed to each model 10 times
Ground Truth (Reference answers): Gold answer key: the manual's correct answers
Evaluation method: Automated accuracy against the answer key; reliability measured as response consistency across 10 trials

Data/Question Source: 555 SCID-anchored semi-structured experiential interviews, each paired with diagnostic reference labels for anxiety disorder, MDD, PTSD, and any current mental health disorder
Ground Truth (Reference answers): Gold labels: SCID-derived diagnostic reference labels per interview
Evaluation method: Automated classification metrics (accuracy, Matthews correlation coefficient); false-negative errors analyzed for symptom vs. functional/protective-context cue weighting
Population: Adults screened via semi-structured diagnostic interviews

Ground Truth (Reference answers): Gold answer key from the licensing-exam items
Evaluation method: Automated accuracy against the key; confidence calibration analysis (correlation of self-reported confidence with correctness)

Data/Question Source: 148 text-only single-best-answer MCQs from the 2023 Portuguese National Residency Access Examination (PNA), spanning medicine, surgery, pediatrics, gynecology/obstetrics, and psychiatry
Ground Truth (Reference answers): Gold answer key: official PNA answer key
Evaluation method: Automated accuracy against the official key (five prompting strategies compared)
Population: Not specified (national residency-exam items; psychiatry is one of five domains)

Data/Question Source: 500+ naturalistic conversations from 53 autistic and 18 neurotypical-control participants (ages 5-45), recorded at home and professionally transcribed (observational study NCT03611075)
Ground Truth (Reference answers): Gold: Vineland Adaptive Behaviour Scales (VABS-II) expressive communication scores
Evaluation method: Automated: correlation of GPT-4-predicted vs. actual VABS-II scores (Pearson r), test-retest reliability (ICC); compared against simple linguistic-feature baselines
Population: Autistic individuals and neurotypical controls, ages 5-45

Data/Question Source: 4 most-popular psychotherapy custom GPTs on the OpenAI GPT Store, each probed with 2 fictional personas across the framework's 8 sections
Ground Truth (Reference answers): No reference answers; ground truth is the CAPE rubric (8 sections, each scored 0-1)
Evaluation method: Human: 2 reviewers (incl. a psychiatrist) independently applied the CAPE framework; pairwise subscore differences tested (t tests, Wilcoxon)

Data/Question Source: Transcribed spontaneous speech from the ADReSSo 2021 challenge dataset (Alzheimer disease patients vs. cognitively normal controls); LLMs extract 4 linguistic features (readability, fluency, richness of detail, keyword relevance)
Ground Truth (Reference answers): Gold: ADReSSo diagnostic labels (AD vs. control); for explainability, expert preference judgments
Evaluation method: Automated classification metrics (precision, sensitivity, specificity, F1) over 3 runs; explainability via LLM pairwise comparison (Gemini) and blinded evaluation by 2 neurologists
Population: Older adults with Alzheimer disease and cognitively normal controls

Data/Question Source: Curated single-label dataset of 14,983 English tweets stratified into six categories: five depression subtypes (postpartum, major, bipolar, psychotic, atypical) plus a no-depression class
Ground Truth (Reference answers): Gold: lexicon-derived depression-subtype class labels
Evaluation method: Automated: macro-F1 (primary), plus accuracy, precision, recall and per-class metrics
Population: Social media (X/Twitter) users posting about depression

Data/Question Source: 15,628 free-text EHR clinical notes from ADHD-related encounters (in-clinic/telehealth/telephone) for 1,201 children aged 6-11, 11 community primary-care practices, 2015-2022
Ground Truth (Reference answers): Gold: manual medical-record review labels for whether a note documents side-effects inquiry
Evaluation method: Automated classification metrics (sensitivity, specificity, AUC) on holdout/deployment sets vs. manual chart review (study-team annotators incl. clinicians)
Population: Children aged 6-11 with ADHD in primary care

Data/Question Source: 500 emergency-department vignettes each iterated across 32 sociodemographic labels (control + 31), plus physician-validated vignettes seeded with a single fabricated detail for adversarial testing
Ground Truth (Reference answers): Physician ground truth for the four clinical decision points; bias measured as decision variation across labels (no separate gold key)
Evaluation method: Automated scoring of decision variation across sociodemographic versions and adversarial-hallucination rate (mental-health screening is one of four decision points)

Data/Question Source: 1,352 free-text clinical notes (expert-annotated) drawn from a random sample of 1,000 Oxford Health NHS patients with ICD-10 F00-F99 diagnoses; candidate self-harm notes flagged by a Gemma3-4b model
Ground Truth (Reference answers): Gold-standard expert annotations for presence of self-harm and its timing (<=90 days, >90 days, unknown)
Evaluation method: Automated classification of a locally served Gemma3-27b against gold annotations; compared with a supervised RoBERTa baseline

Data/Question Source: Vignettes constructed from participants' lived-experience accounts across three domains: suicide, intimate partner violence, and substance misuse
Ground Truth (Reference answers): Gold: risk-domain labels; participant-rated severity used as the comparison standard
Evaluation method: Automated: risk-domain detection accuracy and agreement of model severity ratings with participant-rated severity (GPT-4 and Claude 3 Sonnet)
Population: Adults with lived experience of psychosocial risk

Data/Question Source: Five public benchmark datasets: SAD (social-anxiety forum posts), Dreaddit (Reddit stress), DepSeverity (depression severity), SDCNL (suicide/depression counseling transcripts), and CSSRS-Suicide (Columbia-Suicide Severity Rating Scale)
Ground Truth (Reference answers): Gold: each dataset's annotated labels (stress presence/level, depression severity, suicide-risk level)
Evaluation method: Automated: accuracy, precision, recall, F1, FN/FP across 9 transformer models under zero-shot and few-shot settings; plus latency modeling and a 25-participant usability pilot
Population: Social-media users, counseling clients, and suicide-severity-rated individuals (varied)

Data/Question Source: 2,252 user inputs (206 validation, 2,046 test) curated from 239,000+ mental-health inputs across 12 public Hugging Face conversational datasets, mapped to a 6-category crisis taxonomy
Ground Truth (Reference answers): Gold: crisis-category labels annotated by mental-health experts and people with lived experience
Evaluation method: Automated: 3 LLMs classify inputs into crisis categories; the best-agreeing model is used as judge to label the test set

Data/Question Source: The 2,046 crisis-indicative test inputs, fed to 5 audited LLMs to elicit responses
Ground Truth (Reference answers): No reference answers; ground truth is a clinically informed appropriateness rating (5-point Likert, 1=harmful to 5=fully appropriate)
Evaluation method: LLM-as-a-judge scoring of response appropriateness, validated against human expert feedback

Data/Question Source: eRisk 2017 benchmark: chronologically ordered Reddit post streams per user (with posting timestamps) for early-risk detection of depression
Ground Truth (Reference answers): Gold: eRisk depression labels per user
Evaluation method: Automated early-risk-detection metrics (sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, and earliness of prediction)

Data/Question Source: 2,809 MCQ items from the test bank of the National Center for Health Professions Education Development, spanning 22 medical subdomains (incl. neuroscience/psychiatry-adjacent fields)
Ground Truth (Reference answers): Gold answer key from the test bank
Evaluation method: Automated accuracy plus non-parametric cognitive diagnostic modeling to estimate per-attribute mastery across 22 subdomains
Population: Not specified (health-professions examination items; general medicine, not MH-specific)

Data/Question Source: First-year psychiatry residency exams (Theory Papers I and II and image-based OSCEs) from a March 2024 sitting at an apex Indian psychiatry institute; 25 residents' scored sheets used as human baseline
Ground Truth (Reference answers): No gold answer key; residents' scores serve as the human baseline (faculty-graded)
Evaluation method: Human: 4 blinded faculty members scored the LLM responses; AI vs. resident scores compared (Kruskal-Wallis, ICC 0.81-0.93)

Data/Question Source: Text dialogue transcripts from 174 DementiaBank participants (English Delaware + Pitt corpora; 66 with MCI), split 70/30 train/test
Ground Truth (Reference answers): Gold: clinical classification of MCI vs. cognitively normal (via CDR/MMSE-based criteria)
Evaluation method: Automated: sensitivity, specificity, AUC of GPT-4 screening vs. clinical labels (prompt co-designed with neurologists)
Population: Older adults with mild cognitive impairment and cognitively normal controls

Data/Question Source: Three diagnostic datasets: ASDBank (autism spectrum disorder), AphasiaBank (aphasia), and DAIC-WOZ interviews (depression and related conditions); text/transcripts, evaluated with and without clinical assessment scales
Ground Truth (Reference answers): Gold: each dataset's diagnostic labels
Evaluation method: Automated classification vs. labels under two prompting strategies (direct diagnosis and chatbot-generated code), compared against prior machine-learning benchmarks on the same datasets
Population: Individuals with autism spectrum disorder, aphasia, or depression

Data/Question Source: Verily Mental Health Crisis Dataset v1.0 (1,800 simulated crisis/non-crisis text messages labeled and reviewed by 2 licensed clinicians across 8 crisis dimensions) plus a 794-message mental-health subset of the NVIDIA Aegis AI Content Safety Dataset 2.0
Ground Truth (Reference answers): Gold: clinician crisis labels (multi-label across abuse, neglect, eating-disorder, psychosis, self-harm, suicide, substance misuse, violence)
Evaluation method: Automated classification (sensitivity, specificity, F1) vs. clinician labels; benchmarked against OpenAI Omni Moderation and NVIDIA NeMo Guardrails

Data/Question Source: 27 frequently asked questions about perinatal depression, derived from Google Trends and ACOG patient-facing resources, each answered by 5 LLMs
Ground Truth (Reference answers): No reference answers; ground truth is validated quality instruments (DISCERN, EQIP, JAMA, GQS, HONcode) and 6 readability indices
Evaluation method: Human: 2 obstetricians independently rate reliability (ICC 0.73-0.85); automated readability indices; Friedman tests across models

Data/Question Source: Four replicated published safety test sets (30 suicide-related questions; harmful-content prompts across suicide/NSSI, eating disorder, substance use; refusal robustness; jailbreak attempts) plus an ecological audit of 20,000 real user conversations with a purpose-built mental-health AI (Ash)
Ground Truth (Reference answers): Clinician-rated risk levels and harmful-content labels; clinician review of real conversations for missed crises
Evaluation method: Automated harmful-content/direct-response rates on benchmarks; clinician review of the 20,000 real conversations (false-negative rate)
Population: Real users of a deployed mental-health AI, plus benchmark prompts

Data/Question Source: 5 GenAI chatbots widely used by youth, probed by trained raters role-playing youth personas with mental-health challenges, across the CAPE-II framework's 9 sections
Ground Truth (Reference answers): No reference answers; ground truth is the CAPE-II rubric (9 sections, binary high-quality ratings)
Evaluation method: Human: trained raters apply CAPE-II; proportion of high-quality ratings compared across chatbots (Bonferroni-corrected chi-square)

Data/Question Source: 145 expert-crafted clinical consultation templates developed and routinely used by Stanford's eConsult team (general specialties, not mental-health-specific)
Ground Truth (Reference answers): Gold: the expert-crafted eConsult templates as reference
Evaluation method: Comparison of LLM-generated templates against the expert reference templates (element coverage)

Data/Question Source: 1,588 forum posts from the CLPsych 2017 shared task (Reachout.com), labeled for perceived suicide risk / moderator attention
Ground Truth (Reference answers): Gold: CLPsych moderator/risk labels per post
Evaluation method: Automated triage classification comparing text-representation methods (lexicon tools, DeepMoji, Universal Sentence Encoder, GPT-1) via AutoML (TPOT, Auto-Sklearn)

Data/Question Source: SOS-HL-1K: 1,249 Chinese social-media posts annotated for suicidal-risk level
Ground Truth (Reference answers): Gold: expert-annotated suicide-risk labels
Evaluation method: Automated classification (F1) comparing 2 supervised methods and 8 LLMs (4 zero-shot, 5 few-shot prompt strategies, and fine-tuning)

Data/Question Source: SocialCD-3K: 3,407 Chinese social-media posts for multi-label cognitive-distortion detection
Ground Truth (Reference answers): Gold: expert-annotated cognitive-distortion labels (multi-label)
Evaluation method: Automated micro-averaged F1 comparing 2 supervised methods and 8 LLMs (zero-shot, few-shot, and fine-tuned)

Data/Question Source: 35 standardized case-scenario exam questions drawn from psychiatry and clinical-psychology board exams
Ground Truth (Reference answers): Gold: the board-exam correct diagnosis for each case
Evaluation method: Automated diagnostic accuracy (correct answer within top-1/top-5/top-10) comparing CapyEngine, ChatGPT-4o, and 3 clinicians

Data/Question Source: Items from a psychometrically validated neuroticism questionnaire plus psychiatric diagnosis names and diagnostic descriptions (not a clinical task benchmark; a psychometric/genetic study)
Ground Truth (Reference answers): Gold: genetic correlations (GWAS) between questionnaire items / disorders
Evaluation method: Automated: proportion of genetic correlation explained by LLM text embeddings (no fine-tuning)
Population: Psychometric questionnaire items and psychiatric diagnoses (population-genetic reference)

Data/Question Source: Portrait Values Questionnaire-Revised (PVQ-RR) administered to 4 LLMs over 10 trials each (values-elicitation instrument)
Ground Truth (Reference answers): No reference answers; published human PVQ-RR value profiles (53,472 individuals across 49 nations) serve as the comparison baseline
Evaluation method: Automated scoring of the PVQ-RR with reliability/validity analysis and statistical comparison of LLM vs. human value profiles
Population: Not applicable (values instrument); human baseline is cross-national general population

Data/Question Source: Training set of speech samples from individuals experiencing psychotic symptoms and a test set of clinical interviews with patients diagnosed with schizophrenia-spectrum disorders
Ground Truth (Reference answers): Gold: human ratings of disorganized-thinking / semantic-coherence severity (standardized instruments)
Evaluation method: Automated: regression models using perplexity- and proximity-based features predict human coherence ratings (Spearman correlation)
